Video Call Inspections

Inspected.com · Permit Hub

This guide will walk you through how to join and complete inspections on the Inspected portal — step by step, from login to approval.

Log in to Inspected View steps

Standard process

How to join your inspection

Follow these 4 steps every time you have a scheduled video call inspection.

1

Log in to Inspected

Open your browser and go to inspected.cloud. Sign in with your Inspected credentials.

2

Open the Schedule

Tap the ☰ menu (top-right) and select Schedule.

3

Search for your project

Confirm the date shown matches your inspection date, then type house number only in the search bar and scroll down through results.

Do NOT select inspections marked as Canceled

4

Confirm details & join the call

Verify the appointment time and technician name. Tap the blue Join Call button to connect.

Join Call

If nobody joined past the scheduled time, call your inspector directly.

Required corrections

When an inspection is postponed

If the inspector needs corrections before approving, the inspection is not failed — it is postponed. A new appointment opens automatically.

Original appointment closes

Turns green in the Schedule. Locked — you cannot rejoin it.

New appointment opens

A clock icon appears top-left. Same day (~3–4 PM).

Your action

Reconnect to the new appointment using the same steps 1–4 above.

Original appointment

Closed — circled in green

New appointment

Clock icon — tap Join Call

Remember: The green appointment is permanently closed. Always look for the clock icon to find your new active appointment.

Quick reference

What you see — what to do

Use this table at a glance during any inspection day.

What you seeWhat it meansWhat to do
● Appointment in greenInspection closed / postponedDo nothing
🕐 Appointment with clockNew active appointmentJoin via Join Call

Master Installer
Placard & Photo Guide

Installation requirements, placard standards, and inspection photo checklists for solar interconnection approvals.

For Internal Use · Installation Team Only

1

Introduction

Solar installations require specific safety labels and inspection documentation before a system can receive Permission to Operate (PTO).

This guide provides installers with a clear reference for installing required placards and capturing the inspection photos required by local utilities. Correct labeling and documentation are essential for ensuring that installations meet electrical code requirements and utility interconnection standards.

1.1Purpose of This Guide

The purpose of this guide is to provide installers with a standardized reference for:

Installing required solar safety placards
Capturing the inspection photos required by utilities
Verifying correct labeling before inspection
Reducing delays during the PTO approval process

1.2Utilities Covered

This guide covers placard and inspection photo requirements for three utilities:

SECO Energy
TECO
CenterPoint Energy

1.3When to Use This Guide

Use this guide during the following installation stages:

  • Installing required safety placards
  • Preparing for inspection documentation
  • Capturing photos required for utility submission
  • Verifying system labeling before uploading inspection photos
2

What Is a Placard?

2.1Definition

Placards are safety labels installed on solar systems to notify utility workers, inspectors, and emergency responders that a property contains an interconnected photovoltaic (PV) system. These labels communicate critical information about the electrical system and help ensure safe operation and maintenance.

2.2Functions of a Placard

Safety First

Warn utility workers that the electrical system may still be energized even when the main grid disconnect is open.

Code Required

The NEC and local utility regulations require specific placard types, materials, and placement for interconnected PV systems.

PTO Approval

Utilities will not grant PTO unless all required placards are properly installed and clearly visible in the inspection photos.

System Identification

Clearly identify the presence and location of solar-related electrical equipment so inspectors can quickly understand the system layout.

Emergency Response

During electrical faults, fires, or severe weather, placards provide immediate visual cues that a solar generation system is present.

Future Maintenance

Durable placards help future electricians, inspectors, or property owners understand the system layout even without original project documentation.

3

Placard Standards

3.1Material Requirements

Before installation, all placards must meet minimum material, durability, and visibility standards. These requirements help ensure that labels remain legible, code-compliant, and acceptable for utility inspection.

3.2Accepted Placard Materials

Exterior placards should be made of weather-resistant material. The most commonly accepted type is:

Red phenolic placards with white lettering — designed to remain legible outdoors for long periods and withstand weather exposure.

3.3Unacceptable Placard Materials

The following are not acceptable for permanent installation:

✕
Printed paper labels

Deteriorate quickly, not weather-resistant

✕
Adhesive-only stickers

Peel off over time, fail outdoor exposure

✕
Tape-mounted placards

Temporary — not acceptable for final inspection

4

Types of Placards

4.1Temporary Placards

Temporary placards may be used during early installation stages or inspections when the permanent placard has not yet been mounted.

✕
Not acceptable for final inspection
✓
Must be replaced before PTO approval

4.2Permanent Placards

Permanent placards are required for final sign-off. They must be:

Securely mounted Engraved or permanently bonded Weather resistant Clearly legible

4.3Key Rule: Dual Power Supply Warning Placard

The meter enclosure must always display a DUAL POWER SUPPLY WARNING placard visible from the exterior.
5

SECO Energy — Utility Requirements

5.1Placard Requirements

Before taking inspection photos, verify that all required placards and labels are properly installed:

  • Meter enclosure must display a permanent DUAL POWER SUPPLY WARNING placard visible from the exterior — temporary stickers or paper labels are not acceptable.
  • AC disconnect must display the ON SITE GENERATION UTILITY DISCONNECT SWITCH label.
  • Inside the load center, the solar breaker must include the appropriate NEC warning label indicating the breaker is backfed.

5.2Required Inspection Photos

SECO requires 4 inspection photos to be submitted with the interconnection application. Each photo must clearly show installed equipment and required placards.

1
Meter with Dual Placard SECO

Photo of the utility meter. If it is a dual-feed meter, the enclosure must display a permanent DUAL POWER SUPPLY WARNING placard, not a temporary sticker.

2
Meter with Disconnect SECO

Wide shot showing both the meter AND the on-site generation disconnect switch in the same frame. Labels on the disconnect must be clearly visible.

3
Interconnection Point SECO

Open the load center / main panel and photograph the solar breaker at the point of interconnection. Show any NEC-required warning labels on or next to the breaker.

4
Installed PV Panels SECO

Aerial or elevated shot showing all roof-mounted panels. Panels must be individually countable. Preferred method: drone photography.

5.3Placard Installation Steps

1
Verify Placard Type

Confirm the utility meter uses a permanent DUAL POWER SUPPLY WARNING placard — not a temporary sticker or paper label.

2
Mount on Meter Enclosure

Attach the permanent placard directly on (or adjacent to) the meter socket enclosure, visible from outside. Align level. Use weather-rated hardware.

3
Install Disconnect Label

Affix the ON SITE GENERATION UTILITY DISCONNECT SWITCH label on the disconnect enclosure. Text must be clearly legible — no obstructions.

4
Interconnection Warning

Inside the load center at the solar breaker, attach the required NEC 690 warning labels. For loadside connection: label must read SOLAR ELECTRIC BREAKER IS BACKFED — DO NOT RELOCATE.

5
Photograph All Placards

Take close-up photos ensuring all text is in focus and fully readable. Back up with a wide shot showing context (meter + disconnect in same frame).

6
Upload to Submission Portal

Upload all 4 required photos to the SECO interconnection portal under the correct labeled fields. Blurry or pre-installation photos will be rejected.

5.4SECO Field Checklist

1Placards
  • Permanent DUAL POWER SUPPLY WARNING placard installed on the meter enclosure
  • Placard is red phenolic with white lettering (not a temporary sticker)
  • Placard is mounted on the exterior of the meter enclosure and clearly visible
2Disconnect Labeling
  • ON SITE GENERATION — UTILITY DISCONNECT SWITCH label installed on the AC disconnect
  • Label is clearly visible and legible
  • Label is not obstructed by conduit or equipment
3Panel Labeling
  • Solar breaker inside the load center is properly identified
  • NEC-required warning label installed near the solar breaker
4Required Photos (4)
  • Meter with dual placard clearly visible
  • Meter and AC disconnect shown in the same frame
  • Interconnection point inside panel showing the solar breaker
  • Installed PV panels — all panels visible and countable
5Photo Quality Check
  • Photos taken after installation is complete
  • All labels and placards are readable
  • Equipment is fully visible (not cropped or partially shown)
  • Photos are clear and in focus
6

TECO — Utility Requirements

6.1Placard Requirements

The exterior AC disconnect must display both of the following labels:

RequiredON SITE GENERATION UTILITY DISCONNECT SWITCH
RequiredDANGER / PELIGRO bilingual warning sticker
Note: The ON SITE GENERATION label is separate from the PV AC Disconnect label. Both labels must be present.

6.2Required Inspection Photos

TECO requires 3 inspection photos to be submitted with the interconnection application.

1
Disconnect Switch — On Site Generation TECO

Photograph the exterior disconnect box with the ON SITE GENERATION UTILITY DISCONNECT SWITCH label clearly visible. The DANGER/PELIGRO sticker must also be present and legible.

2
Utility Meter Close-Up TECO

Close-up of the TECO meter showing the full meter face and meter number. Note the CLOCKWISE ABC label below the meter base — this must be visible.

3
Interconnection Point TECO

Wide-angle shot of the entire exterior wall showing the meter, disconnect switch, and any other boxes (sub-panel, gateway, etc.) in a single frame. All warning labels must be readable.

6.3Placard Installation Steps

1
Install On-Site Generation Label

Attach the ON-SITE GENERATION UTILITY DISCONNECT SWITCH label to the exterior disconnect enclosure. This is mandatory for TECO — do not substitute with a generic solar label.

2
Confirm DANGER/PELIGRO Sticker

The DANGER/PELIGRO bilingual warning must be on the disconnect. Verify it is present and undamaged. Replace if faded or torn — it must be photo-ready.

3
Verify Meter Labeling

Check that the TECO meter base has the CLOCKWISE ABC label affixed below. If missing, contact your supervisor — this label is typically installed by TECO, not the installer.

4
Check Exterior Wall Layout

Stand back and confirm the full exterior wall photo will show the meter + disconnect together. If separated by more than 10 ft, document the path between them clearly.

5
Capture All 3 Required Photos

1) Disconnect close-up with label · 2) Meter close-up with meter number visible · 3) Full exterior wall overview. All photos must be in focus and taken post-installation.

6
Submit to TECO Portal

Upload photos to the TECO interconnection portal. Pre-installation photos or images that don't clearly show required labels will result in resubmission delays.

6.4TECO Field Checklist

1Disconnect Labeling
  • ON SITE GENERATION UTILITY DISCONNECT SWITCH label installed
  • DANGER / PELIGRO warning sticker present on the disconnect
2Meter Identification
  • Meter face clearly visible
  • Meter number readable
  • CLOCKWISE ABC label visible below the meter base
3Equipment Layout
  • Meter and disconnect clearly visible on the exterior wall
  • All required warning labels visible in photos
4Required Photos (3)
  • Disconnect switch with ON-SITE GENERATION label
  • Utility meter close-up with meter number visible
  • Full exterior wall overview (meter + disconnect)
5Photo Quality Check
  • Photos taken after installation is complete
  • All labels and placards are readable
  • Equipment is fully visible (not cropped or partially shown)
  • Photos are clear and in focus
7

CenterPoint Energy — Utility Requirements

7.1Placard Requirements

Before submitting inspection photos to CenterPoint Energy, verify that all required solar warning placards and equipment labels are properly installed. Placards must be permanent, weather-resistant, and clearly legible, mounted directly on the corresponding equipment enclosures.

7.2Required Inspection Photos

CenterPoint requires a more extensive set of photos. Installers must submit 12 photo categories through the CenterPoint inspection portal.

1House Number

Photo of the front of the house showing the address number clearly visible.

2Equipment Overview

Wide photo of installed electrical equipment including the CenterPoint meter and AC disconnect. Include directional placard if disconnect is >10 ft from meter.

3Utility Meter

Close-up photo of the CenterPoint utility meter showing the meter face and meter number clearly.

4Main Breaker

Photograph the main service panel — cover installed view and interior with close-up of main breaker rating.

5Overcurrent Protective Devices

If AC disconnect contains fuses, capture a close-up showing the fuse type and rating. Also photograph the combiner panel showing breaker configuration.

6Point of Interconnection

Photo showing where the solar system connects to the electrical service. For line-side taps, show the taps clearly. For loadside, photograph the PV breaker and warning labels.

7AC Disconnect

Photos of the AC disconnect switch — exterior enclosure and interior wiring, ensuring all required warning labels are visible.

8Inverter Nameplate

Close-up photos of the inverter nameplate. For microinverter systems, a clear photo of the microinverter nameplate may be submitted instead.

9Battery Nameplate (if installed)

Close-up of the battery nameplate showing technical specifications, if the system includes a battery.

10Solar Panel Nameplate

Close-up of the solar module nameplate on the back of the panel. All manufacturer information and electrical specifications must be clearly readable.

11Installed PV Panels

Photo showing the entire solar panel array. All panels must be visible and countable. Overhead or drone photo preferred.

12Other Inspection Photos

Additional photos if they help clarify the installation — equipment overview shots, gutter box connections, or sub-panel connections.

7.3Directional Placard Rule

Directional Placard (if required)
Required when the AC disconnect is more than 10 ft from the meter or not visible from the meter.
• The placard must be red phenolic with white lettering, mounted near the meter at eye level.
• Must show the location of the solar panels, meter, disconnect, and the path between them.
ATS/Generator Note: If the residence has an ATS or generator connected, it must be reflected on the one-line diagram and approved by the CNP ATS group prior to being granted PTO.

7.4Placard Installation Steps

1
Assess Disconnect Distance

Check the distance between the AC disconnect and the CenterPoint meter. If the disconnect is more than 10 feet away or not visible from the meter, a directional placard must be installed.

2
Install Dual Power Supply Warning

Attach the WARNING — DUAL POWER SUPPLY SOURCES: UTILITY GRID AND PV SOLAR ELECTRIC SYSTEM label to the exterior of the meter enclosure. The placard must be permanent and weather-resistant.

3
Install AC Disconnect Labels

Verify the AC disconnect displays: exterior label ELECTRIC SHOCK HAZARD / PHOTOVOLTAIC SYSTEM AC DISCONNECT with voltage and current ratings, and interior standard wiring warning label.

4
Install Directional Placard (if required)

If the disconnect is 10 feet or more from the meter, or not in line-of-sight, install a red phenolic directional placard at eye level near the meter. Must include a diagram showing solar array, utility meter, AC disconnect, and path between them.

5
Mark PV Breaker in Load Center

For load-side connections, install the SOLAR ELECTRIC BREAKER IS BACKFED DO NOT RELOCATE label next to the PV breaker. For line-side connections, provide a clear photo of the line taps with the DUAL POWER SUPPLY warning visible.

6
Photograph All 12 Required Categories

Upload all 12 required inspection photos in their corresponding submission fields. Each nameplate photo (inverter, solar module, battery if installed) must be a clear close-up with all specifications readable.

7.5CenterPoint Field Checklist

1Placards
  • DUAL POWER SUPPLY WARNING placard installed on meter enclosure
  • Placard is permanent and weather-resistant (red phenolic)
2Directional Placard (if required)
  • AC disconnect distance verified
  • Directional placard installed if disconnect is 10 ft or more from the meter
  • Diagram shows meter, disconnect, solar panels, and path between them
3Electrical Labeling
  • PV breaker labeled: SOLAR ELECTRIC BREAKER IS BACKFED DO NOT RELOCATE (load-side)
  • Required AC disconnect warning labels visible
4Required Photos (12)
  • House number visible
  • Equipment overview (meter + AC disconnect)
  • Utility meter close-up
  • Main breaker panel — cover + interior
  • Overcurrent protective devices / fuses
  • Point of interconnection
  • AC disconnect (exterior + interior)
  • Inverter nameplate
  • Battery nameplate (if installed)
  • Solar panel nameplate
  • Installed PV panels — all panels countable
  • Other relevant equipment photos
5Photo Quality Check
  • Photos taken after installation is complete
  • All labels and placards are readable
  • Equipment is fully visible (not cropped or partially shown)
  • Photos are clear and in focus
8

Final Considerations

8.1Utility Comparison Table

Requirement SECO Energy TECO CenterPoint
Permanent placard on meter✓ Required✓ Required✓ Required
Temporary placard allowed✕ No✕ No✕ No
On-Site Generation disconnect label✓ Required✓ Required✓ Required
DANGER / PELIGRO sticker— N/A✓ Required~ Case-by-case
Directional placard rule~ Case-by-case~ Case-by-case✓ Required if >10 ft
Required inspection photos43+12
Meter number must be visible—✓ Yes✓ Yes
Nameplate photos required——✓ Yes
Interconnection photo required✓ Yes—✓ Yes

8.2Common Mistakes to Avoid

These are the most common causes of PTO delays:

  • ✕Using temporary stickers instead of permanent placards
  • ✕Submitting blurry inspection photos
  • ✕Forgetting the directional placard for CenterPoint when disconnect >10 ft
  • ✕Missing inverter, panel, or battery nameplate photos
  • ✕Uploading photos that do not clearly show labels or equipment
